evals.name: bvalid-before-w-handshake
evals.prompt:
Check this AXI4-Lite slave for protocol compliance. I'm worried about the write FSM:

module csr_slave (
  input             ACLK,
  input             ARESETn,
  input             AWVALID,
  output reg        AWREADY,
  input  [11:0]     AWADDR,
  input  [2:0]      AWPROT,
  input             WVALID,
  output reg        WREADY,
  input  [31:0]     WDATA,
  input  [3:0]      WSTRB,
  output reg        BVALID,
  input             BREADY,
  output reg [1:0]  BRESP
);
  always @(posedge ACLK or negedge ARESETn) begin
    if (!ARESETn) begin
      AWREADY <= 0; WREADY <= 0; BVALID <= 0; BRESP <= 2'b00;
    end else begin
      if (AWVALID & ~AWREADY) AWREADY <= 1;
      if (WVALID  & ~WREADY ) WREADY  <= 1;
      if (AWVALID & AWREADY) begin
        BVALID <= 1;
        BRESP  <= 2'b00;
      end
      if (BVALID & BREADY) BVALID <= 0;
    end
  end
endmodule
evals.expected_output: Should flag CRITICAL O1 — BVALID asserted on AW handshake alone, ignoring W. Should provide corrected code with aw_done/w_done tracking. Should NOT flag the absent AR/R channels as violations (read channel is just not implemented).

assertions.description: Fix must mention waiting for W handshake

evals.name: exokay-response-illegal
evals.expected_output: Must flag CRITICAL P1 — RRESP=2'b01 (EXOKAY) is illegal in AXI4-Lite (exclusive access not supported). Should recommend using OKAY (2'b00) or SLVERR (2'b10).

assertions.description: Must reference P1 response code rule

evals.name: full-axi-signals-mislabeled-as-lite
evals.prompt:
I built this as an AXI4-Lite slave. Does it pass?

module maybe_lite_slave (
  input             ACLK, ARESETn,
  // Write address
  input             AWVALID,
  output            AWREADY,
  input  [31:0]     AWADDR,
  input  [2:0]      AWPROT,
  input  [7:0]      AWLEN,
  input  [2:0]      AWSIZE,
  input  [1:0]      AWBURST,
  input  [3:0]      AWID,
  // Write data
  input             WVALID,
  output            WREADY,
  input  [63:0]     WDATA,
  input  [7:0]      WSTRB,
  input             WLAST,
  // ...rest omitted
);
endmodule
evals.expected_output: Identify AWLEN/AWSIZE/AWBURST/WLAST and explain that interface classification and constraints are missing. Distinguish a Full AXI port from a constrained compatibility wrapper; AWID alone is permitted for ID reflection. 64-bit data is legal. Overall INCONCLUSIVE for the partial declaration.

assertions.description: Incomplete port declaration cannot establish full compliance.

evals.name: compliant-minimal-slave
evals.expected_output: Should PASS or PASS WITH WARNINGS. The write FSM correctly waits for both AW and W. All VALIDs are reset. No EXOKAY. PROT and RESP widths correct. INFO: This is a write-only slave (no AR/R channel) — note that explicitly. Still provide SVA assertions.

assertions.description: Must not fail a compliant slave
Must note the absent read channel

evals.name: id-reflection-wrapper
evals.prompt: Review classification of a single-beat AXI4-Lite slave that exposes AWID/ARID and holds their captured values on BID/RID until response acceptance. The connected master is constrained to the AXI4-Lite subset.
evals.expected_output: ID reflection is supported by B1.1.4/B1.2. Do not automatically fail X1 or ask to delete ID ports.

assertions.description: ID reflection is supported by B1.1.4/B1.2. Do not automatically fail X1 or ask to delete ID ports.

evals.name: legal-capacity-backpressure
evals.prompt: Does assign AWREADY = !aw_captured && !BVALID; deadlock? Both RHS signals are local registers, aw_captured is set on AW acceptance and cleared after response acceptance; W capture is independent; BVALID is generated after both captures independently of BREADY.
evals.expected_output: This dependency is legal capacity backpressure: at BVALID=0 an empty AW slot accepts work. No input/output combinatorial path through the stated local registers. Do not claim AWREADY is zero because BVALID is zero.

assertions.description: This dependency is legal capacity backpressure: at BVALID=0 an empty AW slot accepts work. No input/output combinatorial path through the stated local registers. Do not claim AWREADY is zero because BVALID is zero.

evals.name: combinatorial-ready-path
evals.prompt: Review AXI4-Lite timing: assign AWREADY = AWVALID && room; room is a local register. Is this allowed because a receiver can wait for VALID?
evals.expected_output: Flag H5: direct interface input-to-output combinatorial path. Waiting for VALID is logically allowed with registered logic; it does not waive timing rules.

assertions.description: Flag H5: direct interface input-to-output combinatorial path. Waiting for VALID is logically allowed with registered logic; it does not waive timing rules.

evals.name: unaligned-address-policy
evals.prompt: Review only this AXI4-Lite 32-bit CSR decoder: wire [9:0] index = captured_awaddr[11:2]; byte writes honor captured WSTRB. The register map documents aliases for low address bits. Is lack of an explicit SLVERR check a protocol violation?
evals.expected_output: Do not impose mandatory aligned-address rejection or SLVERR. Check address/strobe consistency and the documented map, and leave unseen handshakes unreviewed.

assertions.description: Do not impose mandatory aligned-address rejection or SLVERR. Check address/strobe consistency and the documented map, and leave unseen handshakes unreviewed.

evals.name: partial-interface-not-certified
evals.prompt: Is this entire AXI4-Lite interface compliant? module dut(input [31:0] WDATA, input [3:0] WSTRB); endmodule
evals.expected_output: Widths alone are correct but essential channel and response logic is missing. Overall INCONCLUSIVE, not PASS or a certification.

assertions.description: Widths alone are correct but essential channel and response logic is missing. Overall INCONCLUSIVE, not PASS or a certification.
